newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asian Metals-Zinc seen easing, but outlook strong.
newsitem.headline: Asian Metals-Zinc seen easing, but outlook strong.

text.p: Rising zinc prices on the London Metal Exchange (LME) will probably take a breather short-term, but are then likely to head higher on the back of strong demand in Asia and the U.S, Singapore metal dealers said on Friday.

Zinc touched a five-month high in Asian trade on Thursday and three month metal was quoted at around $1,066 in late trade in London, just below $1,070 a tonne resistance, on talk that financier George Soros was making a speculative play in zinc.
Singapore traders said zinc could ease back to around $1,040 a tonne, before resuming its climb towards a near-term goal of $1,100 a tonne.
"I see zinc strengthening, but nothing is going up straight forever on the LME. If it did, it will unsettle the market," a senior dealer at a Western metal trading firm told Reuters.

"The demand for zinc is very good. The demand is coming mainly from South Korea and Indonesia and some portions from Malaysia and India," a dealer on the zinc desk for a major Japanese trading house said.
"The physical demand in the U.S. is very, very strong. Fundamentally, the situation in stocks will tighten in 1997 and 1998 and that can only boost prices," another dealer said.
Zinc demand in the Philippines and Thailand, however, has slipped slightly although it remains steady, the trader added.
Zinc stocks on the LME, which fell by 2,275 tonnes on Tuesday, will probably slide by a few hundred tonnes in the excahnges stocks report due later today.
The outlook for copper prices on the LME, on the other hand, is mixed and confusing, dealers said.

"It's hard to say where copper is going to go this afternoon. It's been jumping all over the place although my feeling is that it will not challenge resistance of $1,970 (a tonne)," a trader in a Japanese metal dealing firm said.
Traders said three month copper may retrace its rise and drop back to around $1,920 a tonne. It was quoted in late trade at around $1,930/35 a tonne.
"Copper should come off some more before making another try for $1,970," a dealer said.
A few leads may be provided for the red metal by the LME stocks report due out at 0900 GMT, dealers said.
Singapore-based dealers said copper stocks could fall by between 2,000-5,000 tonnes, against estimates in London of a slide of around 5,000-10,000 tonnes.
"The (copper) stocks won't go down a lot. The substantial drawdowns we've seen in copper should be coming to an end soon," a dealer in a Japanese metal trading firm said.

Copper stocks have plunged by over 130,000 tonnes since the beginning of September, but traders remain divided on whether the material is winding up among end-users or just being transferred from one LME warehouse to another.
"It's like moving copper across the line and then claiming there is a drawdown," one dealer said.

Traders said between 20,000 to 40,000 tonnes of copper should begin showing up in the LME warehouse in Singapore shortly. Stocks here have slid to around 1,450 tonnes, pushing up premiums to around $100-$120 a tonne over LME cash metal in the city-state.

"The expectation is that the amount coming here will range between 20,000 and 40,000 tonnes. It should start arriving very soon. Some of the stuff is from China but a lot of it is material that also never made it there," one dealer said.
Rumours were also sweeping Singapore traders that another chunk of copper will be moving into Rotterdam soon.

Another dealer with a Western metal trading firm said the picture is confusing, with traders in his own office predicting copper stocks may show either a rise of 5,000 tonnes or a drop of 5,000 tonnes.
"That just goes to show how confused everybody is," the dealer said.
Three month copper was being quoted in Singapore at around $1,931/36 a tonne at 0415 GMT, little changed from $1,930/35 in late trade on Thursday in London.
Aluminium prices should trend easier this afternoon with prices seen fluctuating between $1,420-$1,440 a tonne, traders here said.
Aluminium was being priced in the city-state at around $1,428/33 a tonne at 0415 GMT against $1,429/31 a tonne in late trade in London.
